questions.content: Giving five points, explain the effects of the Earth’s rotation.

media.alt: Unchanged original Geography question paper page 10.
Unchanged original Geography question paper page 11.
Unchanged original Geography question paper page 12.

questions.answerKey: (1) Day and night: places alternately face toward and away from sunlight. (2) Apparent daily movement of the Sun and stars: as Earth turns eastward, celestial objects generally appear to move westward across the sky. (3) Local solar-time differences: different longitudes face the Sun at different moments. (4) Coriolis deflection: rotation causes large-scale moving air and water to be deflected to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere. (5) Equatorial bulge/polar flattening: rotation contributes centrifugal effects that make Earth slightly oblate. These are distinct explained effects; tides are mainly due to differential lunar/solar gravity and should not be credited simply as an effect of rotation.
questions.markingGuide: Question10 is the only question in SectionC, printed as15 marks. Independent SomaSmart rubric (not an official NECTA scheme): for each of five distinct valid effects, give1 mark for correctly identifying the effect and up to2 additional marks for a correct causal explanation (0–3 per point, total0–15). Do not double-count the same effect expressed twice. Accept scientifically valid alternatives. Written answers remain pending until self-assessed.
